title: finding(app-shell): a flow that ends `refused` WITHOUT a screen pause never opens FlowRunner — the launch handlers return success and the action toasts `successMessage`, so the refusal is never shown
body:
Dedup keywords: `flow launch refusal swallowed` · `refused outcome without screen pause` · `interpretFlowResponse done arm` · `useConsoleActionRuntime flowHandler` · `AutomationResult refusalMessage`

Surfaced by the `os-dev` implementing objectui#7707 (PR objectui#9971) as an `out_of_scope_findings` entry, and filed by the dispatching `domain:ui#2` execution seat. ⛔ Ungraded and ⛔ unrouted beyond the lane label — priority and type are the triage seat's.

## The defect

A flow that ends with `outcome: 'refused'` **without ever pausing at a screen** never opens `FlowRunner` at all. The two console launch handlers therefore fall through to their terminal-success tail and return `success: true`; `ActionRunner` then toasts the invoking action's `successMessage`, and **the authored refusal sentence is never shown to anyone**.

⇒ the user asks for something, the platform evaluates the rule and says no, and the screen says the action succeeded.

## Why it is two filing classes at once

**(a) reproducible defect** — the path is ordinary: any flow whose `end` node declares `outcome: 'refused'` and which reaches that node without a screen pause.

**(b) breach of a declared contract** — the maintainer ruling on objectstack-ai/objectstack#14945 (director seat, decision batch #42) says a runner renders the refusal with **Close only** and **no completion toast**. Here there is no Close, no message, and there IS a completion toast. The contract names `AutomationResult.refusalMessage` as the carrier, and on this route nothing reads it.

## Why objectui#7707 did not fix it, on purpose

That card is **leg (3)** of the ruling and names `FlowRunner`. The `silent` clause it must not touch — a paused run returns `{success: true, silent: true}` so the invoking action's toast is suppressed — describes the **paused** launch route, which is the only route `FlowRunner` sees. This finding is the **unpaused** route, which never reaches the component that card is about. PR objectui#9971 leaves it untouched deliberately, and the seat agrees: widening that PR to cover a second route would have made a fenced delivery into an unfenced one.

## Where a fix would land (named by the reporting dev, ⛔ not re-measured by this seat)

The two console launch handlers — `useConsoleActionRuntime`'s flow handler and `RecordDetailView`'s — and the `done` arm of `interpretFlowResponse` in `packages/app-shell/src/utils/flowResponse.ts`, which after PR objectui#9971 can distinguish `refused` from `completed` but is only consulted on the route that opens the runner.

⚠️ ⛔ The seat has NOT re-measured any line of this section, and ⛔ has not reproduced the defect itself: it is relayed from the dev's report with attribution. The first step for whoever takes this card is to reproduce it — a flow with a `refused` end and no screen node — and to say what it measured, ⛔ not to build from this paragraph.

## Not a sub-issue

⛔ Not filed under objectui#7707 and ⛔ not under any queued card: the fix lands in launch handlers that card's fence excludes by construction.
